# Independent PGF spacing, minima and anchors

These files were generated by actual **PGF 3.1.11a**, through pdfTeX
3.141592653-2.6-1.40.29 (TeX Live 2026). The generator imports only the independent
case inventory; it never imports production geometry, support tables or MathJax.
Each body is a fixed TeX box with width 20pt, height 8pt and depth 3pt, except
the recorded deep-text and zero-axis cases. It records actual current em/ex
dimensions separately.

Regenerate from the repository root:

```sh
PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH npm run generate:point-anchor-references
PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH node --test tests/geometry/pointNodeAnchorReferences.test.ts
```

`STZ_PDFLATEX` overrides the engine path. The script uses `-no-shell-escape`,
retains compilation output and records source hashes, engine/version and command
in `references.json`. It targets the recorded TeX Live 2026 PGF source paths; if
using another installation, update the explicit paths only after verifying the
same source version/hashes. The geometric library hash is
`bbd6abe9df51153e2f4f61cca3ad669de34a6648cf37795df44da931402b69ee`;
the basic-shape module hash is
`01dd81e3f2c56a8db7864916ada1a5036964aff2e8176aafd4773244e236bb27`.
The same manifest records and authenticates seven sources, including core
points/transforms, scalar arithmetic, trigonometric tables and cylinder's bounded
line/arc bisection.

`fixed-box.tex` is the complete input. `geometry.txt` is PGF's raw soft-path
tokens and anchor output, in TeX pt. `references.json` reverses only the y sign
for SVG comparison; it does not use CSS px, PDF bp or 72pt/in. The test authenticates
input/raw hashes, all 172 unique cases, fifteen shape identities and 4,925 anchor
observations. Named shape anchors, every configured polygon/star index and nine
numeric direction spellings are included in each applicable profile.

Anchor tolerance is 0.025 TeX pt; the maximum observed residual is 0.022225pt
(dart with width minimum, north west). Contour tolerance is 0.03pt
because the largest semicircle has radius 80pt:
PGF's cubic-circle approximation differs from an analytic arc by up to
0.000273r, separately from the production boundary sampling's 0.005-unit sagitta.
The original 32C fixtures continue to pass their unchanged 0.025pt comparison.
Negative controls detect wrong circle diameter, independently stretched
triangles, displaced text origin and ignored outer separation.

Positive outer separation follows PGF's diamond exception: it shrinks the
painted contour by `(sqrt(2)-1)*sep` while expanding anchor axes. Negative outer
separation reverses that effect. Other shape paint remains independent of outer
clearance. Cylinder negative inner ysep is excluded from successful references
because PGF itself terminates in an out-of-domain inverse sine; valid negative
inner xsep remains in the cylinder negative profile. Runtime geometry rejects
that singular branch with a retained-source diagnostic.

All fifteen shapes include strong negative outer separation (-30pt on both
axes). Their clearance can invert. PGF preserves signed compass radii and its
declared angle comparisons, selecting infinite border lines; a nearest positive
ray gives different results. Cylinder uses PGF's bounded angular bisection even
when the declared arc is not crossed. Zero-axis ellipse cases retain PGF's
zero-vector normalization. Numeric border angles become integer counts through
`pgfmathsetcounter`: unsigned/leading-plus literals truncate their integer prefix,
while leading minus uses TeX dimensional rounding before count truncation.
Positive literals require an integer prefix; negative leading-dot decimals use
the full parser. The raw spelling is retained, including long fractions near the
scalar limit. Polar math rejects counts at 16,384 degrees; negative values can
fail earlier when dimensional rounding reaches TeX's maximum dimension.

`failures/` retains separate TeX inputs, command output and partial geometry for
eleven expected upstream failures: negative-inner-y cylinder fitting, zero-axis
diamond numeric direction, strong-negative sector directions 45 and south west,
deep-negative kite numeric -30, four numeric range errors and two positive
leading-dot forms. Their nonzero statuses and primary PGF failures are
authenticated in the manifest. The other 23 anchors of that sector case compile
successfully and remain usable; an unused invalid anchor cannot invalidate the
selected one. Strong negative inner separation and rotated negative clearance
include fixed-box controls for the signed sector-center offset and nearly
parallel kite/trapezium edges. TeX's scalar scanning, product truncation and
rounded affine inverse are preserved rather than increasing tolerance.

These fixed-box comparisons establish geometry/anchor conformance only.
Native App, actual MathJax/font readiness, click-time settled downloads and
standalone SVG reopening require their separate parent browser evidence.
